titulo: Me and you: Introductions and the accusative with «зовут»

aula.objetivo: Introduce yourself, use the 8 personal pronouns and complete the Cyrillic alphabet.

blocos.explicacao: GROUP 4 — Truly new letters (and new sounds). Here is the group that takes effort. There are eight letters with a new shape and a new sound. You really have to memorise them. I will explain each one calmly: Ж — like the «s» in «measure» Ж is the «zh» sound, as in «measure», «vision» or the «g» in «genre». It looks like a butterfly or an insect. жена́ → zhee-NAH (wife) журна́л → zhoor-NAHL (magazine) жизнь → zheezn (life) Ц — like the «ts» in «cats» Ц is the «ts» sound at the end of «cats» or «pizza». It looks like a «U» with a little tail. цена́ → tsee-NAH (price) центр → tsentr (center) коне́ц → kah-NYEHTS (end) Ч — like the «ch» in «chat» Ч is the «ch» sound of «chair». It looks like a «4». час → chahs (hour) чай → chy (tea) челове́к → chee-lah-VYEK (person) Ш — like the «sh» in «shop» Ш is the «sh» sound of «ship» and «shop». It looks like three vertical strokes joined at the bottom. шко́ла → SHKOH-lah (school) шапка → SHAHP-kah (hat) шум → shoom (noise) Щ — a longer, softer «sh-ch» Щ is a longer «sh» followed by a light «ch», as in «fresh cheese» said quickly. It looks like a «Ш» with a little tail. щи → shchee (cabbage soup) борщ → borshch (beet soup) това́рищ → tah-VAH-reeshch (comrade) Ъ — the hard sign (no sound) Ъ is a sign that has no sound of its own. It separates a consonant from a vowel, keeping the consonant hard. It appears in few words. объе́кт → ab-YEKT (object) объясни́ть → ab-yas-NEET (to explain) съесть → syest (to eat up) Ы — the throaty «ee» Ы is the hardest sound for English speakers. Say «ih» as in «bit», then pull your tongue back and down while keeping your lips relaxed and spread, not rounded. мы → mih (we) вы → vih (you) сын → sihn (son) ры́ба → RIH-bah (fish) Tip: say «ee», then pull your tongue back without moving your lips. The result is roughly «ы». Ь — the soft sign (no sound) Ь is a sign that has no sound of its own. It softens the consonant before it. That is, the consonant that comes before it is pronounced with a very light «y» after it. день → dyen' (day) ночь → noch' (night) мать → maht' (mother) слова́рь → slah-VAR' (dictionary) Tip: imagine you are saying the word and, at the end, you sketch a very light «y». That is it.

blocos.titulo: The alphabet table and phonetic spelling
blocos.explicacao: The full table of the Russian alphabet. Here is the complete alphabet, in the correct order. Look at the columns: Note: the Cyrillic order is its own; it is inherited from the Greek alphabet. The big insight: the Russian alphabet is PHONETIC. Here is the most important thing in this lesson. Pay attention. In English, the same letter can have many sounds. Take the C: cat → «k» sound, city → «s» sound, church → «ch» sound, ocean → «sh» sound. Take «ough»: though, through, rough, cough, bough — five different sounds. This is a nightmare even for people learning English. But Russian is different. In Russian, each letter almost always has one fixed sound. Learn the letter, learn the sound. Full stop. There are two exceptions (we will see them in the next section), but they are predictable exceptions. Russian is much more phonetic than English. This is one of the reasons Russian is easier for an English speaker than it looks. You do not need to guess the pronunciation: you read it.

blocos.titulo: The two pronunciation rules you need to know now
blocos.explicacao: The two pronunciation rules you need to know now. There are two pronunciation rules that show up from the very beginning. You need to learn them now. Rule 1: Unstressed «О» becomes «А» In Russian, the letter О sounds like «o» only when it is stressed (with the stress mark). When it is unstressed, it sounds like «a». Examples: This is why you will see spellings such as «mahsk-VAH» and «mah-lah-KOH» in books. That is the real pronunciation. Russians do not say «mohsk-VAH», they say «mahsk-VAH». What to do: when you learn a new word, learn it with the stress mark. Without the stress mark, you do not know whether the «o» is «o» or «a». Keep the word with its stress. Rule 2: Voiced consonants at the end become voiceless In Russian, if a word ends in a voiced consonant (Б, В, Г, Д, Ж, З), it is pronounced as the corresponding voiceless consonant (П, Ф, К, Т, Ш, С). Examples: This is why you will see spellings such as «drook» and «GOH-raht». That is the real pronunciation. Russians do not say «droog», they say «drook». What to do: when you learn a word, listen to the pronunciation. With time, your ear takes over.

blocos.explicacao: To say your name in Russian you use «зовут» (they call) + a pronoun in the accusative, the object form (me, you, him, her, us, them). Literally: «me they call…».

blocos.enunciado: Say your name aloud using «Меня зовут…». Then ask an imaginary friend: «Как тебя зовут?»
Listen and write: я, ты, вы, он, она, мы.
